changelog: Add a core principle warning against cutting between a verb and its essential complement and describing what a GOOD cut looks like, to address the primary finding that the prompt underestimates how tightly verbs bind to complements.

Replace C4 to address the primary finding: emphasize verb+complement cohesion and describe what a GOOD cut looks like (end after a complete predicate or clause closer) rather than only penalizing cuts.
Replace E1 with measured example cmn_hans_cn_605 to teach the model about cuts that split predicate + complement (保持 不变).
Replace E2 with measured example cmn_hans_cn_982 to show cuts that separate verb phrases (需 要 / 小 心 蚊 子) in short-latency pairs.
Replace E3 with measured example cmn_hans_cn_1099 to expose predicate-complement splits around verb+object (脱 落) in medium-latency cases.
Replace E4 with measured example cmn_hans_cn_362 to illustrate harmful cuts that separate comparative/resultative constructions (还 要 小).

Replace C5 to address the primary finding: emphasize that verb+complement and related predicate frames are tight units and describe what a GOOD cut looks like (prefer cutting after a completed predicate or clause-closer rather than imposing a blanket ban).
